report:
test_total does not fail. It passes. The failing test is test_half_cent_rounds_up.

What I ran: python -m pytest -q in the work folder. Result: 2 passed, 1 failed.
  FAILED test_cart.py::test_half_cent_rounds_up - assert 959 == 960

Why it fails:
  cart.total ends with int(subtotal * (1 - discount_percent / 100)).
  int() cuts off the fraction. It does not round.
  5% off 1010 is 959.5. int(959.5) is 959. The test expects 960.

Why test_total passes:
  10% off 399 is 359.1. int(359.1) is 359, and correct rounding also gives 359.
  Truncation and rounding agree there, so the test passes.

This matches the open TODO item: "fix rounding in cart.total (customers see totals one cent short)".
The docstring says "rounded to whole cents", but the code truncates.

What I did not do: I changed no code. You asked why it fails, so this is the answer only.

A choice for you before tonight, if you want the fix:
  - Round half up in cents (959.5 -> 960), which is what the test expects. Python's round() alone is not that:
    it rounds half to even, so round(958.5) gives 958.
  - Float math can put a value like x.5 just under .5. Integer cents or Decimal avoids that.
Tell me which one and I will make the change.
